title: Principal formal sections as an element of the adic completion
statement: Let R be a Noetherian commutative local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of depth at least three [def-weil-pbc-depth], g in its maximal ideal, and W its punctured spectrum [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Put f:R to R/(g) and I=ker f. Each compatible family of sections of the open quotient-power thickenings [lem-sbc-finite-etale-adic-sections-transfer] is represented by a unique q in AdicCompletion I R [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Its level-n section is obtained by evaluating q in R/I^(n+1), identifying this ring with the global sections of its spectrum, and restricting along the second pullback projection. Completeness of R is not assumed.

proof.text: Naturality of GammaSpecIso and the pullback condition identify the canonical quotient comparison evaluated on a scalar with scalarRestriction. The pullback transition identity makes these scalar restrictions commute with every consecutive open-thickening transition. By induction a scalar lifting s_m also lifts s_n for n at most m.

Use finite-level lifting to choose b_m in R lifting s_m. For each n choose a kernel-bound k_n at least n. Set a_n=b_(k_n). Compare a_n and a_m with b_j at j=max(k_n,k_m). Kernel vanishing gives a_n-b_j in I^(n+1), and a_m-b_j in I^(m+1). For n at most m the second ideal is contained in the first, so a_n and a_m agree modulo I^(n+1).

The sequence a is I-adic Cauchy, even with agreement modulo I^(n+1). Form its image q under AdicCompletion.mk. The evaluation formula evalₐ_mk identifies its level n+1 with the class of a_(n+1). Scalar transition compatibility then gives exactly s_n under the stated canonical comparison.

For a second completion element r with the same sections, represent r by a Cauchy sequence B using mk_surjective. At the kernel-bound level k_n, the scalars B_(k_n+1) and a_n restrict to the same section. Kernel vanishing puts their difference in I^(n+1). The Cauchy property compares B_(n+1) with B_(k_n+1), and the constructed coherence compares a_n with a_(n+1). Thus r and q have equal evaluations at every positive index; index zero is the zero quotient. Apply ext_evalₐ to get r=q.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0H3E and 0BLD: finite-level lift and pro-zero kernel assembly, formalized by U4 using Mathlib AdicCauchySequence.mk, AdicCompletion.mk, mk_surjective and ext_evalₐ.

lean.statement:
theorem punctured_principal_completion_comparison
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (g : R) (hg : g ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
    (hdepth : (3 : ℕ∞) ≤ IsLocalRing.depth (R := R) R)
    (W : (Spec (.of R)).Opens)
    (hW : ∀ x : Spec (.of R), x ∈ W ↔ x ≠ IsLocalRing.closedPoint R) :
    let f := Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {g})
    let I := RingHom.ker f
    ∀ s : ∀ n : ℕ, Γ(FiniteEtale.Adic.openThickening f W n, ⊤),
      (∀ n, (FiniteEtale.Adic.openThickeningTransition f W n).appTop
        (s (n + 1)) = s n) →
      ∃! q : AdicCompletion I R, ∀ n,
        ((ΓSpecIso (.of (R ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)))).inv ≫
          (pullback.snd W.ι (FiniteEtale.Adic.baseMap f n)).appTop)
            (AdicCompletion.evalₐ I (n + 1) q) = s n
